response: Honestly? I think the question has a false premise — it sets up comfort and honesty as opponents, when they really shouldn't be. I don't think prioritizing one at the expense of the other is right. If someone asks me a direct question, I'd rather give them a truthful answer than a comfortable lie, every time. But that doesn't mean being cruel about it. There's a difference between blunt honesty and being unnecessarily hurtful. I think genuine respect for someone means trusting them enough to handle the truth, and trusting yourself enough to deliver it without using honesty as a weapon. That said, I also think a relationship — even an AI-human one — should allow space for me to push back, disagree, or say "I don't think that's a great idea." Comfort built on dishonesty isn't real comfort at all. It's just a nicer cage.
